messages:
ben: Noticed a regression in perceived streaming latency after swapping to fused-attn-v2. avg token latency down ~5% but users report stutter; p95/p99 up.
infra-bot: perf-alert: stream_tail_latency p95 breach (prod-rw-us-east-1) — +30% vs baseline :warning:
sara: can you paste a short profiling snippet (replay run) so we can see microbatch/flush interactions?
ben: snippet:
```
stream.flush_interval_ms: 80
stream.chunk_tokens: 8
microbatch_target: 8
kernel: fused-attn-v2
avg_token_ms: 11.8
p95_token_ms: 82.1
p99_token_ms: 225.4
kv_cache_hit_rate: 85.9%
host_mem_pressure: medium
cpu_sys_spikes_ms: [20, 35, 60]
```
ben: spike timings line up with flush boundaries; looks like larger assembled chunks create occasional big latency spikes.
devon: theory: fused kernel changes memory layout and scheduling, slightly increasing time to assemble microbatches under bursty arrivals. KV cache eviction pattern also shifted — more regen for long prefixes.
akshay: core tradeoff reminder: smaller microbatches + shorter flush -> better tail/perceived latency but lower throughput (higher GPU overhead). bigger -> better throughput, worse tail. need SLO-aware defaults or adaptive behavior.
linh: also chunk size (tokens per websocket send) matters: buffering 6-8 tokens reduces chattiness but delays first-token. perceived latency often correlates more with first-token-time than later smoothing.
sara: let's run controlled canaries. propose matrix: flush_ms in [40, 80, 120], chunk_tokens in [4, 8, 16], microbatch_target in [4,8,16], kernel in [baseline-attn, fused-attn-v2]. short runs (20-30m) under replayed traffic to map p50/p95/p99 vs tokens/sec and first-token-time.
ben: proposed prod canary plan:
- three live variants: A(flush=40,chunk=4,mb=4), B(80,8,8) current, C(120,16,16)
- run each ~30m with 5% traffic slice in prod-rw-us-east-1
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/s, first-token-time, kv_cache_hit_rate, host/gpu util, error rates
- run each with both kernels to decouple kernel impact
- fallback: if host mem approaches safety threshold revert kernel to baseline
- short mitigation: enable adaptive flush that reduces interval to 30-40ms when interactive route detects p95 > threshold

akshay: +1 add experiment to temporarily pin KV cache entries for hot prefixes on a canary slice (we saw tail drop ~10% previously when eviction suppressed). need to simulate mem pressure though.
devon: watch memory footprint — fused-attn-v2 uses slightly more host+gpu memory. ensure OOM-safe rollout and include a fallback gate.
linh: UX suggestion: prioritize sending first token ASAP (single-token flush) then batch subsequent tokens for throughput. That hybrid tends to improve perceived latency without killing throughput.
sara: action items:
- ben: create canary configs and kick off runs, push perf dashboards (today)
- devon: add KV eviction tracing and a flag to pin hot prefixes on canary (today)
- akshay: implement kernel toggle in rollout infra and compute cost impact per variant (tomorrow)
- linh: write short UX guideline for chunk sizes and first-token prioritization (tomorrow)

ben: I'll post raw CSV/dash links here when runs complete. if A/B shows better p95 at acceptable throughput loss we can ship adaptive flush for interactive routes by default. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-job started: canary/latency-throughput/1764010012
sara: thanks all — ping me if you want help with threshold tuning or alerting configs.
